heroText: Open Simon Says on a laptop at the meeting table and press Start. While you talk, your own Google Doc fills up with decisions, who does what and what you're discussing right now. We never touch what you write yourselves.
freeLine: Free for associations in Linköping. Swedish, English and everything in between.
step1Text: The person running the meeting confirms that everyone knows the meeting is transcribed and can ask for a pause. Only then can you press Start.
step2Text: The laptop's own microphone is enough. A short name round first, so it says Anna and Erik instead of Speaker 1 and Speaker 2.
step3Text: About once a minute the notes are updated: decisions, to-dos with names and dates, and what's being discussed. The full transcript is in a tab of its own.
editsTitle: We never touch what you write yourselves.
editsText: The secretary can write in the document throughout the meeting. Correct an item and it's locked: Simon Says writes around it, but never changes or removes your text. Not even in the summary when the meeting is over.
factsTitle: Made for a room full of people
fact1Text: The built-in microphone is enough. Nothing to install, no extra microphone to buy.
fact2Text: Even when someone switches language mid-sentence.
fact3Text: One button. No audio is sent until you press Resume.
fact4Text: The document is created in the Google Drive of the person who starts the meeting and shared with the association's members.
limits: Free: up to 20 hours a month per association and 4 hours per meeting. Open source on <repo>GitHub</repo>, and how things are going right now is on the <status>status page</status>.
closeText: Create the association, invite the board and put the laptop on the table.
demoLabel: Example: a meeting document being filled in during the meeting
demoCaption: Example. This is what the document looks like while you talk. Notes are written in the meeting's language (Swedish for now).
